name: Beauty Hacks
_comment_group: One more show under the Snapchat heading. The heading names the
network these frames are cut FOR and the channel is the show they are
cut from, so another show cutting for the same network is one more
folder under it rather than a heading of its own.
Like every channel under this heading it is a frame fetcher rather
than a thumbnail maker: a video goes in and a numbered grid of
vertical stills comes out, each captioned with what was being said
over it.
It is cut to Hall of Femme's design, and that pack is the one to read
first: the frame fetch, the 540x960 vertical output, the
transcription, the rewrite, the card at the foot of the frame, the
palette handed to the user, the highlight that changes FACE and not
colour - all of it is Hall of Femme's and is named here rather than
restated. What makes this show itself is one sentence long: it is set
in Proxima Nova Bold with picked words in Proxima Nova Black, on a
magenta card, in four colours offered for the type and the same four
for the card.
It is not a second skin for Beauty-Tipps, which sorts next to it and
shares half a word with it. That show has no card at all: Syne
Regular with picked words in Bebas Neue, one deep violet, a white
halo, set straight onto the photograph. This one was cut from Hall of
Femme on the instruction that it follow that pack, so it keeps the
card, keeps the palette and keeps the two-face highlight. Two shows
about the same subject are not two colourways of one pack, and a
change to either is not a change to the other.
The id is kebab-case ASCII because it is also the folder name and the
key everything else refers to; the name is the brand.
_comment_capture: The frame fetch, whole, from content/presets/snapchat-capture.json:
the slider's range, the 540x960 output, the transcription, and the
rewrite that turns it from speech into report. This channel has
nothing to say about any of it that its neighbours do not.
_comment_title: Where this show parts company with the pack it was cut from, which is
in the type and in the colours and nowhere else. Hall of Femme sets
its captions in Telegraf - a 200-weight hairline for the block, the
800 for a picked word - on a hot pink card, in sixteen pairings the
user chooses between. This one is set in Proxima Nova, Bold for the
block and Black for a picked word, on a magenta card, in sixteen
pairings of a white, a black and two magentas.
Everything else - the size, where the lines break, the capitals, the
freeform text box, the shape of the card, its padding and corners and
shadow, where the block stands on the frame, the drag - is the
Snapchat caption design and is stated once, in
content/presets/snapchat-caption.json. This pack states only what
makes it this show, which is the whole of what a pack under this
heading should be.
The type here is heavy where Hall of Femme's is thin, and that quietly
removes the risk its note spends a paragraph on. A 200-weight face
needs the card or it disappears on a blown-out sky; a 700 would
survive without one. The card is kept anyway, and for a better reason
than inheritance: it is the magenta, and the magenta is the brand. On
this show the card is the shape that is a fifth of the frame and reads
before anything on it, so it is what carries the colour, and the type
is what has to stay legible against it.

_comment_face: Proxima Nova Bold. Which cut that is, why the full name rather
than 'Proxima Nova' is declared, and what the machine may already
know it by are written out in
The Bold and not the Black - the lighter of the two cuts this
pack carries - and the choice is made HERE rather than in the
highlight below: whichever cut the block takes, a picked word has
the other one, and an emphasis goes heavier than what surrounds
it - the way every other pack under this heading goes heavier.
Setting the block in the heaviest cut there is leaves the emphasis
nowhere to go but down, which is what this pack used to do and
Capitals come from the preset and cost this face nothing: it is a
geometric grotesque whose capitals are what it is usually seen in,
and the two cuts share a cap height, so at the preset's 40px they
stand 26.7px tall - within a tenth of a pixel of the Telegraf the
design was measured on, so a caption here occupies the same band
of frame as one on the pack next door.
_comment_color: The channel's own answer, and therefore what every frame is set in
until somebody presses a swatch: a frame stores no colour of its
own until it is given one, and this is what it falls back to (see
state.textColorFor). It is the first of the four in `colors`
below, so the white swatch is the one that shows as chosen on an
untouched frame - though nothing requires that, and the swatch is
found by matching this value rather than by being listed first.
White letters on the magenta card is the pairing this show opens
on, and it is the pairing to open on rather than merely the first
one written down. White on #FF00F0 is 3.2 to 1, which is thin for
type in general and sound for this type in particular - a
700-weight grotesque set at 40px, which is the case the 3:1
large-text threshold exists to describe. Black on the same card is
6.5 to 1 and is a button away for anyone who wants it.
_comment_colors: The four colours this show is set in, offered for the letters and
for the card behind them - four buttons each in the title panel
(see editor.renderColorButtons).
The same four in both lists, which is what every pack under this
heading that offers a palette does and for their reason: the point
is the PAIRING. Sixteen combinations of a white, a black, a
magenta and a violet-magenta, and the ones worth having are the
ones that read. A palette that could only ever be used one way
round would be a palette of four cards, and this show's look is
the pairing rather than any one of them.
Written in the order the show states its colours in - the two
neutrals, then the two brand colours - and the two defaults are
picked out of it by value rather than by position: the type opens
on the first entry and the card on the third. That is the freedom
Hall of Femme's note describes, used here to keep both rows in one
order.
Nothing stops the user setting #FF00F0 on #BB15D9, and that is the
one pairing in this palette worth knowing about before somebody
reports it: at 1.5 to 1 the two magentas are near enough the same
value that a caption in one on a card of the other is a caption
nobody can read. It is left available all the same, for the reason
the packs either side give about white on white - the two lists
are independent because the pairing is the feature, and a rule
barring the combinations that fail would cost the panel more
explaining than an invisible caption costs a user who can see it
is invisible and presses another swatch.
`text` reaches the highlight as well as the block - see the note
on `colors` in js/channels.js. This channel's highlight is a
different CUT of the face and not a different colour, so what
colour the type is has one answer and not two.
_comment_highlight: A picked word is set in Proxima Nova Black, in the same colour as
the rest of the block. The highlight here is WEIGHT, which is Hall
of Femme's highlight exactly - one family's cuts on one card, so
the card stays one clean shape instead of a shape with a second
shape inside it - with one difference from it that is worth
stating plainly.
The pair used to be the other way round: the block in the Black
and a picked word stepping DOWN to the Bold, on the argument that
what the eye catches is the change of weight and not its
direction. That was asked for and then asked back, and the reason
is the one the argument left out - a step down makes the picked
word the thinnest thing on the card rather than the thickest,
which is an odd place for the word that was worth picking out, and
it is backwards from every other pack under this heading. It
climbs now, 700 to 900, the way Hall of Femme climbs 200 to 800.
The step is a short one whichever way it runs. 700 against 900 of
one family is two adjacent weights, where 200 against 800 is the
family's two ends: THE VERDICT WAS GUILTY measures 495px in the
Bold and 511px in the Black at 40px, 3.2% apart, against the 11.4%
Telegraf's two cuts put between the same string. So a picked word
here changes the colour of the stroke and almost nothing about the
shape of the line. It is a quieter highlight than the pack this was
cut from, and on a short caption read at arm's length it is close
to the quietest a highlight can be and still be one. Two faces were
named and these are the two; if it ever wants to be louder, the
honest fix is a third cut of the family rather than a box - see the
preset, where the argument for a recolour over a box lives.
The colour it names is the block's, so the recolour draws exactly
what its neighbours are drawn in and the face is the whole of the
difference. Stated all the same, for the fallback reason `color`
above is stated - a highlight that changed colour as well as
weight would be two highlights.
Both cuts have the same cap height, the same ascender and the same
descender, so the shared vertical band every box in the block takes
is the band the Bold alone would have asked for. A caption with
picked words in it is exactly as tall as one without.
No shadow stated, so the preset's null stands: these letters are on
a solid card in a colour the user picked, and the card casts the
one shadow there is.
The mode and the scope come from the preset, which is where the
argument for picking out words rather than lines lives.
_comment_panel: Magenta, and the fill is the one thing about the card this pack
decides: its shape, its padding, its corners and its shadow are the
Snapchat caption design and come from the preset.
It is the third entry in `colors.panel` above rather than the
first, which is the same freedom `color` uses at the other end of
the row - the swatch that shows as chosen is found by matching this
value and not by being listed first, so both rows can be written in
the order the show states its colours in while the channel still
opens on white type and a magenta card.
#FF00F0 and not Hall of Femme's #FF008A. They are the same idea one
step apart on the wheel - that pink is a red-magenta and this is a
true one - and the step is what makes this a different show at a
glance rather than the same show in a slightly different pink.

_comment_branding: No dark gradient. It exists to hold a title legible against the
photograph, and this title is not against the photograph at all - it
is on a card of its own. A scrim over every still would darken forty
pictures to solve a problem the card has already solved.
